## What's new

**Updating no longer makes the app disappear.** Pressing the install button used to hand the
package to Installer.app and leave the sheet frozen — the button said "Install & Relaunch" and
delivered neither. Now the app installs the update, waits until the new version is genuinely on
disk, and offers a **Relaunch Now** button so the restart happens when you are ready. If the
privileged service is not responding it says so and gives you a working fallback instead of a
dead end.

**"What's New" is populated again.** 1.0.2 shipped with an empty panel: the release notes were
written to GitHub but never inlined into the update manifest. The release tooling now fails
loudly rather than shipping a blank changelog.

---

## 🔒 The update manifest is now signed

`updates.json` was the one unsigned link in the update chain. The installer package was signed
and verified, but the document that says *which* package to install was trusted on HTTPS alone.

It now carries an Ed25519 signature, verified against the same key compiled into the app. The
filename is part of the signed digest, so a package signature cannot be replayed as a manifest
signature.

If the signature is missing or does not verify, updates still work exactly as before — discovery
is unaffected, because the package signature was always the real gate. What an unsigned manifest
loses is *authority*: WGSmart 1.0.3 can mark a release as required, and it will only honour that
instruction from a manifest it has authenticated. That ordering is deliberate — an unauthenticated
document must never be able to disable anyone's software.

Nothing in this release is marked required.

---

## 🐧 Linux

**Fixed: the apt package could not start.** The `.deb` installed the binary to `/usr/bin` while
the systemd unit it shipped pointed at `/usr/local/bin`, so `systemctl start wgsmart-hub` failed
with `status=203/EXEC`. This affected every 1.0.2 apt install. Both paths are now `/usr/bin`, and
upgrading removes the stale copy. If you installed 1.0.2 via apt, this is the fix you need.

**The browser UI now ships.** `wgsmart-webbff` was written but never packaged — enabling it meant
a Go toolchain and hand-written systemd units. It is now in both the tarball and the `.deb`.

```sh
sudo wgsmart-webui-enable          # apt
sudo ./install.sh --with-web       # tarball
```

It is **off until you turn it on**, binds loopback only, and runs as an unprivileged account —
it is an HTTP login in front of a root daemon, so none of that is automatic. Reach it over an
SSH tunnel, or put a TLS proxy in front; `WEBUI.md` covers both, in English, Tiếng Việt and 中文.

On the same machine it talks to the hub over its Unix socket with no certificates at all. That is
stronger than a token, not weaker: the socket is `0600` and every connection is checked with
`SO_PEERCRED`, so the kernel attests the caller's uid. Managing a hub on a *different* machine
still uses TLS 1.3 with mutual TLS and/or a bearer token.

**Smaller downloads.** Linux binaries are built with symbols stripped — about 31% off each. Even
with the web UI added, the `.deb` is smaller than 1.0.2's hub-only package.

---

## Still true, and worth repeating

- **Not notarized.** macOS will warn on first launch. The warning is accurate: this build is
  ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed. Right-click ▸ Open, or clear the quarantine attribute.
- **App routing on macOS is per-UID**, not per-process. It routes everything a given user runs,
  which is the honest description of what the mechanism does.
- **The Linux hub is young.** It builds and its tests pass, and the packaging bugs above are the
  kind that only surface on a real machine. Read the install guide before putting it on a server
  that matters.
- Windows is not supported.

## Verifying this download

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c WGSmart-1.0.3.pkg.sha256
```

The `.sig` files are Ed25519 signatures over the same artifacts; the app checks them
automatically on every update.
